name: Paracetamol
description: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is a pain reliever and a fever reducer.
uses: Relief of mild to moderate pain (headache, muscle ache, toothache).
Reduction of fever.
dosage: 500mg to 1000mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 4000mg in 24 hours.
precautions: Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Consult a doctor if you have liver disease.

name: Amoxicillin
description: Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic that fights bacteria.
uses: Treatment of bacterial infections (ear infections, pneumonia, skin infections).
Used in combination with other medications to treat stomach ulcers caused by H. pylori.
dosage: As prescribed by a doctor, usually 250mg to 500mg every 8 hours.
precautions: Complete the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better. Do not use if allergic to penicillin.

name: Ibuprofen
description: Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).
uses: Reducing fever and treating pain or inflammation caused by many conditions such as headache, toothache, back pain, arthritis, or minor injury.
dosage: 200mg to 400mg every 4 to 6 hours. Do not exceed 1200mg in 24 hours unless directed by a doctor.
precautions: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Consult a doctor if you have heart or kidney problems.

name: Cetirizine
description: Cetirizine is an antihistamine that reduces the natural chemical histamine in the body.
uses: Treating cold or allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching, watery eyes, or runny nose.
dosage: 5mg to 10mg once daily.
precautions: May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you.

name: Metformin
description: Metformin is an oral diabetes medicine that helps control blood sugar levels.
uses: Used together with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage: As prescribed by a doctor, usually taken with meals.
precautions: Monitor blood sugar levels regularly. Consult a doctor if you have kidney disease.

name: Omeprazole
description: Omeprazole decreases the amount of acid produced in the stomach.
uses: Treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
Healing of erosive esophagitis.
Treatment of stomach ulcers.
dosage: 20mg to 40mg once daily before a meal.
precautions: Long-term use may increase the risk of bone fractures. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist.

name: Azithromycin
description: Azithromycin is an antibiotic that fights bacteria.
uses: Treatment of many different types of infections caused by bacteria, such as respiratory infections, skin infections, ear infections, and sexually transmitted diseases.
dosage: 500mg once daily for 3 days, or as directed by a doctor.
precautions: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium within 2 hours of taking azithromycin.

name: Atorvastatin
description: Atorvastatin is used to lower cholesterol and triglycerides in the blood.
uses: Lowering the risk of stroke, heart attack, and other heart complications in people with type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease, or other risk factors.
dosage: 10mg to 80mg once daily.
precautions: Avoid grapefruit juice. Consult a doctor if you have liver disease or experience unexplained muscle weakness.

name: Amlodipine
description: Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker that dilates blood vessels and improves blood flow.
uses: Treatment of high blood pressure (hypertension).
Treatment of chest pain (angina).
dosage: 5mg to 10mg once daily.
precautions: Avoid alcohol. Consult a doctor if you experience severe dizziness or fainting.

name: Salbutamol (Ventolin)
description: Salbutamol is a bronchodilator that relaxes muscles in the airways and increases air flow to the lungs.
uses: Treatment or prevention of bronchospasm in people with reversible obstructive airway disease.
Prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm.
dosage: 1 to 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed.
precautions: Seek medical help if your usual dose does not provide relief.

name: Ciprofloxacin
description: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections.
uses: Urinary tract infections
Respiratory tract infections
Skin infections
Bone and joint infections
dosage: 250mg to 750mg every 12 hours.
precautions: Drink plenty of fluids. Avoid excessive sunlight or UV lamps.

name: Losartan
description: Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure.
uses: Hypertension
Reducing risk of stroke in patients with hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy
dosage: 25mg to 100mg once daily.
precautions: Do not use during pregnancy. Monitor kidney function regularly.

name: Dexamethasone
description: Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used to treat conditions such as arthritis, blood/hormone disorders, and allergic reactions.
uses: Severe allergic reactions
Arthritis
Asthma
Certain cancers
dosage: As prescribed by a doctor (dosage varies widely).
precautions: May mask signs of infection. Do not stop suddenly if used long-term.

name: Furosemide (Lasix)
description: Furosemide is a loop diuretic (water pill) used to treat fluid retention (edema) in people with congestive heart failure, liver disease, or kidney disorder.
uses: Edema
Hypertension
dosage: 20mg to 80mg per day.
precautions: May cause potassium loss; may require potassium supplements.

name: Prednisolone
description: Prednisolone is a steroid that prevents the release of substances in the body that cause inflammation.
uses: Allergic disorders
Skin conditions
Ulcerative colitis
Arthritis
Lupus
Psoriasis
Breathing disorders
dosage: 5mg to 60mg per day depending on condition.
precautions: Avoid people who are sick or have infections. Long-term use can lead to bone loss.

name: Clopidogrel (Plavix)
description: Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet medication that prevents blood clots.
uses: Prevention of heart attack and stroke in people with heart disease
Recent stroke
Peripheral vascular disease
dosage: 75mg once daily.
precautions: Inform your doctor or dentist before any surgery.

name: Gliclazide
description: Gliclazide is an oral hypoglycemic (anti-diabetic drug) used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes.
uses: Control of blood sugar in type 2 diabetes
dosage: 30mg to 120mg once daily with breakfast.
precautions: Always carry a source of sugar in case of hypoglycemia.

name: Ranitidine
description: Ranitidine is an H2 blocker that reduces the amount of acid your stomach produces.
uses: Heartburn
Acid reflux
Stomach ulcers
dosage: 150mg twice daily or 300mg once at bedtime.
precautions: Consult a doctor if symptoms persist.

name: Pantoprazole
description: Pantoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that decreases the amount of acid produced in the stomach.
uses: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
dosage: 20mg to 40mg once daily.
precautions: Best taken 30-60 minutes before breakfast.

name: Multivitamins
description: Multivitamins are used to provide vitamins that are not taken in through the diet.
uses: Vitamin deficiencies caused by illness, pregnancy, poor nutrition, digestive disorders, and many other conditions
dosage: One tablet daily.
side_effects: Unusual or unpleasant taste in your mouth
precautions: Do not exceed the recommended dose.

name: Decolgen
description: Decolgen is a combined medication for the relief of cold and flu symptoms.
uses: Relief of symptoms associated with common cold, flu, and allergic rhinitis.
Relief of headache, fever, nasal congestion, and sneezing.
dosage: Adults: 1 tablet every 6 to 8 hours, or as prescribed by a doctor.
precautions: May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery. Avoid alcohol.

name: Biogesic
description: Biogesic is a popular brand of Paracetamol for pain and fever relief.
uses: Relief of mild to moderate aches and pains such as headache, toothache, and muscular aches.
Reduction of fever.
dosage: Adults: 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours, not to exceed 8 tablets in 24 hours.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have liver or kidney problems. Do not take with other Paracetamol-containing products.

name: Panadol
description: Panadol is a widely used brand of Paracetamol for pain relief.
uses: Effective relief of headache, muscle pain, period pain, toothache, and sore throat.
Reduction of fever.
dosage: Adults: 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed.
precautions: Do not take with other medicines containing paracetamol. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist.

name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
description: ORS is a mixture of electrolytes and sugar used to prevent or treat dehydration.
uses: Prevention and treatment of dehydration caused by diarrhea, vomiting, or excessive sweating.
dosage: Dissolve one sachet in 250ml or 1 liter of clean water (as specified on the packet) and drink as needed.
precautions: Use clean, boiled water to dissolve the salts. Discard unused solution after 24 hours.

name: Domperidone (Motilium)
description: Domperidone is an anti-sickness medicine used to treat nausea and vomiting.
uses: Relief of nausea and vomiting.
Relief of stomach discomfort, bloating, and belching.
dosage: Adults: 10mg up to 3 times a day, usually before meals.
precautions: Not recommended for people with heart conditions. Consult a doctor before use.

name: Loperamide (Imodium)
description: Loperamide is used to treat sudden diarrhea.
uses: Symptomatic relief of acute diarrhea.
Management of chronic diarrhea in inflammatory bowel disease.
dosage: Initial dose 4mg, followed by 2mg after each loose stool, not to exceed 16mg in 24 hours.
precautions: Do not use if you have bloody stools or fever. Maintain hydration with ORS.

name: Diclofenac (Voltaren)
description: Diclofenac is an NSAID used to reduce pain and inflammation.
uses: Relief of pain and inflammation in arthritis, gout, and acute musculoskeletal disorders.
Post-operative pain relief.
dosage: Adults: 50mg to 150mg daily in divided doses, or as prescribed.
precautions: Take with food. Not recommended for people with stomach ulcers or heart disease.

name: Aspirin
description: Aspirin is used to reduce fever, pain, and inflammation.
uses: Relief of mild to moderate pain.
Prevention of blood clots in heart disease (low dose).
dosage: Adults: 300mg to 900mg every 4 to 6 hours for pain. 75mg daily for heart health (low dose).
precautions: Do not give to children under 16 due to risk of Reye's syndrome. Avoid if you have asthma or stomach ulcers.

name: Enervon-C
description: Enervon-C is a multivitamin supplement containing Vitamin C and B-complex.
uses: Boosting the immune system and providing energy.
Treatment of vitamin deficiencies during periods of stress or illness.
dosage: Adults: One tablet daily.
precautions: Do not exceed the recommended daily dose.

name: Chlorpheniramine (Burmeton)
description: Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms.
uses: Relief of sneezing, itchy and watery eyes, and runny nose caused by hay fever or common cold.
Relief of itchy skin rashes and hives.
dosage: Adults: 4mg every 4 to 6 hours.
precautions: Highly sedating; avoid driving or operating machinery. Avoid alcohol.

name: Metronidazole (Flagyl)
description: Metronidazole is an antibiotic used to treat various infections caused by bacteria and parasites.
uses: Treatment of infections of the digestive system, skin, and joints.
Treatment of dental infections and infected leg ulcers.
dosage: Adults: 200mg to 400mg three times a day for 3 to 10 days.
precautions: Do not drink alcohol during treatment and for 48 hours after finishing the course.

name: Mefenamic Acid (Ponstan)
description: Mefenamic acid is an NSAID used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain.
uses: Relief of period pain and heavy bleeding.
Relief of toothache, muscle pain, and joint pain.
dosage: Adults: 500mg three times a day after meals.
precautions: Take with food. Not suitable for people with stomach ulcers or asthma.

name: Cefixime (Zifi)
description: Cefixime is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections.
uses: Treatment of urinary tract infections, ear infections, and throat infections.
Treatment of bronchitis and gonorrhea.
dosage: Adults: 200mg to 400mg daily, as a single dose or divided into two doses.
precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or other cephalosporins.

name: Loratadine (Claritin)
description: Loratadine is a non-drowsy antihistamine used to treat allergy symptoms.
uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes caused by hay fever.
Treatment of hives and itchy skin rashes.
dosage: Adults: 10mg once daily.
precautions: Generally non-drowsy, but use caution if performing tasks requiring alertness.

name: Salbutamol Inhaler (Ventolin)
description: Salbutamol is a bronchodilator that opens up the airways in the lungs.
uses: Relief of symptoms of asthma and COPD.
Prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm.
dosage: 1 or 2 puffs as needed, up to 4 times a day.
precautions: If your usual dose does not provide relief, seek emergency medical help immediately.

name: Gaviscon
description: Gaviscon is an antacid and alginate used to treat acid reflux and indigestion.
uses: Relief of heartburn and acid indigestion.
Treatment of symptoms of hiatus hernia and reflux oesophagitis.
dosage: 10-20ml or 1-2 tablets after meals and at bedtime.
precautions: Avoid taking other medicines within 2 hours of taking Gaviscon.

name: Vitamin B-complex (Neurobion)
description: Neurobion is a combination of B vitamins (B1, B6, B12) used to support nerve health.
uses: Prevention and treatment of vitamin B deficiencies.
Support for nerve health and treatment of neuritis.
dosage: One tablet daily or as directed by a doctor.
precautions: Do not exceed the recommended dose. Consult a doctor for prolonged use.

name: Ferrous Sulfate (Sangobion)
description: Sangobion is an iron supplement with vitamins and minerals to treat iron-deficiency anemia.
uses: Treatment and prevention of iron-deficiency anemia.
Supplementation during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
dosage: One capsule daily after meals.
precautions: Best taken on an empty stomach, but can be taken with food if it causes stomach upset.

name: Azithromycin (Zithromax)
description: Azithromycin is a macrolide antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections.
uses: Treatment of respiratory infections, skin infections, and ear infections.
Treatment of some sexually transmitted diseases.
dosage: Adults: 500mg once daily for 3 days, or as directed by a doctor.
precautions: Do not take antacids containing aluminum or magnesium at the same time.

name: Albendazole (Zentel)
description: Albendazole is an anthelmintic medication used to treat a variety of parasitic worm infestations.
uses: Treatment of tapeworm, roundworm, and hookworm infections.
Treatment of pinworm infections.
dosage: Adults: Usually 400mg as a single dose. Some infections may require a longer course.
precautions: Avoid use during pregnancy. Consult a doctor before giving to children.

name: Atenolol
description: Atenolol is a beta-blocker used to treat high blood pressure and heart-related chest pain.
uses: Treatment of hypertension (high blood pressure).
Prevention of angina (chest pain).
Treatment of irregular heartbeats.
dosage: Adults: 25mg to 100mg once daily, or as prescribed.
precautions: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly. Consult your doctor first.

name: Enalapril
description: Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure.
uses: Treatment of high blood pressure.
Management of heart failure.
dosage: Adults: 5mg to 40mg daily, usually divided into one or two doses.
precautions: May cause a dry cough. Inform your doctor if you experience swelling of the face or throat.

name: Glibenclamide (Daonil)
description: Glibenclamide is a sulfonylurea medication used to treat type 2 diabetes.
uses: Control of blood sugar levels in type 2 diabetes.
dosage: Adults: 2.5mg to 15mg daily, usually taken with breakfast.
precautions: Monitor blood sugar regularly. Carry a source of sugar in case of hypoglycemia.

name: Sitagliptin (Januvia)
description: Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor used to treat type 2 diabetes.
uses: Improving blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes.
dosage: Adults: 100mg once daily, with or without food.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have a history of pancreatitis or kidney problems.

name: Fluconazole (Diflucan)
description: Fluconazole is an antifungal medication used to treat various fungal infections.
uses: Treatment of vaginal, oral, and esophageal yeast infections.
Treatment of fungal meningitis.
dosage: Adults: 150mg as a single dose for vaginal yeast infections. Other doses vary by infection.
precautions: Inform your doctor if you have liver disease or heart rhythm disorders.

name: Carbocisteine (Solmux)
description: Carbocisteine is a mucolytic that helps thin and loosen mucus in the lungs.
uses: Relief of cough associated with excessive mucus.
Treatment of respiratory tract disorders like bronchitis and asthma.
dosage: Adults: 750mg three times a day initially, then reduced as symptoms improve.
precautions: Avoid use if you have a history of stomach ulcers. Consult a doctor if cough persists.

name: Bromhexine (Bisolvon)
description: Bromhexine is a mucolytic agent used to treat respiratory disorders associated with productive cough.
uses: Thinning and loosening phlegm in the airways.
Relief of chest congestion.
dosage: Adults: 8mg to 16mg three times a day.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have stomach ulcers or liver/kidney problems.

name: Kremil-S
description: Kremil-S is a combination of antacids and simethicone used to treat stomach issues.
uses: Relief of stomach pain, heartburn, and acid indigestion.
Relief of gas and bloating (flatulence).
dosage: Adults: 1 to 2 tablets after meals and at bedtime, or as needed.
precautions: Do not take more than 12 tablets in 24 hours. Consult a doctor for long-term use.

name: Betamethasone (Skin Cream)
description: Betamethasone is a potent corticosteroid used topically to reduce skin inflammation and itching.
uses: Treatment of eczema, psoriasis, and dermatitis.
Relief of itchy and inflamed skin rashes.
dosage: Apply a small amount thinly to the affected area 1 or 2 times daily.
precautions: Do not use on the face, groin, or underarms unless directed by a doctor. Avoid long-term use.

name: Clotrimazole (Canesten)
description: Clotrimazole is an antifungal medication used to treat skin and vaginal fungal infections.
uses: Treatment of athlete's foot, ringworm, and jock itch.
Treatment of vaginal yeast infections (thrush).
dosage: Apply to the affected area 2 to 3 times daily for 2 to 4 weeks.
precautions: Continue treatment for 1-2 weeks after symptoms disappear to prevent recurrence.

name: Povidone-iodine (Betadine)
description: Povidone-iodine is an antiseptic used to prevent infection in minor wounds.
uses: Disinfection of minor cuts, scrapes, and burns.
Pre-operative skin preparation.
dosage: Apply to the cleaned affected area as needed.
precautions: Do not use over large areas of the body. Consult a doctor if the wound is deep or severe.

name: Simvastatin
description: Simvastatin is used to lower cholesterol and triglycerides in the blood.
uses: Lowering high cholesterol and triglycerides.
Reducing the risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart complications.
dosage: 10mg to 40mg once daily in the evening.
precautions: Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice. Report unexplained muscle pain to your doctor.

name: Rosuvastatin (Crestor)
description: Rosuvastatin is a statin medication used to lower cholesterol and prevent cardiovascular disease.
uses: Lowering LDL (bad) cholesterol and increasing HDL (good) cholesterol.
Slowing the build-up of plaque in blood vessels.
dosage: 5mg to 20mg once daily.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have liver disease or persistent muscle weakness.

name: Bisoprolol (Concor)
description: Bisoprolol is a beta-blocker used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure.
uses: Treatment of hypertension.
Management of chronic heart failure.
dosage: 1.25mg to 10mg once daily.
precautions: Do not stop taking abruptly. May mask symptoms of low blood sugar in diabetics.

name: Telmisartan (Micardis)
description: Telmisartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure.
uses: Treatment of hypertension.
Reduction of cardiovascular risk in patients unable to take ACE inhibitors.
dosage: 40mg to 80mg once daily.
precautions: Do not use during pregnancy. Monitor kidney function and potassium levels.

name: Spironolactone (Aldactone)
description: Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic used to treat fluid retention and high blood pressure.
uses: Treatment of edema in heart failure or liver cirrhosis.
Treatment of high blood pressure.
Treatment of primary hyperaldosteronism.
dosage: 25mg to 100mg daily.
precautions: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium.

name: Montelukast (Singulair)
description: Montelukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist used to prevent asthma attacks and treat allergies.
uses: Maintenance treatment of asthma.
Relief of symptoms of seasonal and year-round allergies.
dosage: 10mg once daily in the evening.
precautions: Not for the treatment of acute asthma attacks. Report any mood or behavior changes.

name: Theophylline
description: Theophylline is a bronchodilator used to treat symptoms of asthma and other lung diseases.
uses: Relief and prevention of symptoms of asthma, chronic bronchitis, and emphysema.
dosage: As prescribed (dosage requires careful monitoring of blood levels).
precautions: Limit caffeine intake. Many drugs interact with theophylline; consult your doctor.

name: Lansoprazole (Prevacid)
description: Lansoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that reduces stomach acid.
uses: Treatment of stomach and intestinal ulcers.
Treatment of GERD and erosive esophagitis.
dosage: 15mg to 30mg once daily before a meal.
precautions: Consult a doctor if symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks of use.

name: Hyoscine Butylbromide (Buscopan)
description: Hyoscine butylbromide is an antispasmodic used to relieve cramps in the stomach and intestines.
uses: Relief of stomach cramps, period pains, and symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
dosage: 10mg to 20mg three to four times daily.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have glaucoma or an enlarged prostate.

name: Ondansetron (Zofran)
description: Ondansetron is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by surgery, chemotherapy, or radiation.
uses: Prevention of nausea and vomiting.
dosage: 4mg to 8mg every 8 to 12 hours as needed.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have a history of heart rhythm problems (QT prolongation).

name: Levothyroxine (Thyroxin)
description: Levothyroxine is a synthetic thyroid hormone used to treat an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).
uses: Replacement therapy for hypothyroidism.
Treatment of goiter.
dosage: As prescribed by a doctor, usually taken on an empty stomach 30-60 minutes before breakfast.
precautions: Requires regular blood tests to monitor thyroid levels. Do not switch brands without consulting your doctor.

name: Glimepiride (Amaryl)
description: Glimepiride is a sulfonylurea used to control blood sugar in type 2 diabetes.
uses: Lowering blood sugar levels in type 2 diabetes.
dosage: 1mg to 4mg once daily with breakfast.
precautions: Monitor blood sugar regularly. Carry a sugar source for emergencies.

name: Pioglitazone (Actos)
description: Pioglitazone is a thiazolidinedione used to improve blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes.
uses: Improving insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes.
dosage: 15mg to 45mg once daily.
precautions: Not recommended for people with heart failure or bladder cancer history.

name: Cephalexin (Keflex)
description: Cephalexin is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections.
uses: Treatment of respiratory, skin, bone, and urinary tract infections.
dosage: 250mg to 500mg every 6 hours.
precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin.

name: Doxycycline
description: Doxycycline is a tetracycline antibiotic used to treat various infections and acne.
uses: Treatment of respiratory, urinary, and skin infections.
Treatment of acne and prevention of malaria.
dosage: 100mg once or twice daily.
precautions: Avoid taking with dairy products, antacids, or iron supplements. Stay out of direct sunlight.

name: Clindamycin
description: Clindamycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by bacteria.
uses: Treatment of serious respiratory, skin, and soft tissue infections.
dosage: 150mg to 450mg every 6 hours.
precautions: Report severe or persistent diarrhea to your doctor immediately.

name: Clarithromycin (Klacid)
description: Clarithromycin is a macrolide antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections.
uses: Treatment of respiratory tract infections, skin infections, and stomach ulcers (with other drugs).
dosage: 250mg to 500mg every 12 hours.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have heart rhythm disorders or liver/kidney disease.

name: Acyclovir (Zovirax)
description: Acyclovir is an antiviral medication used to treat infections caused by herpes viruses.
uses: Treatment of cold sores, shingles, and chickenpox.
Management of genital herpes.
dosage: 200mg to 800mg multiple times daily depending on the infection.
precautions: Start treatment as soon as possible after the first symptoms appear. Drink plenty of water.

name: Ketoconazole (Nizoral)
description: Ketoconazole is an antifungal medication used to treat fungal infections of the skin.
uses: Treatment of athlete's foot, ringworm, and seborrheic dermatitis (dandruff).
dosage: Apply cream 1-2 times daily. Use shampoo 2 times a week.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes. Consult a doctor for oral use due to risk of liver damage.

name: Gabapentin (Neurontin)
description: Gabapentin is used to treat nerve pain and certain types of seizures.
uses: Relief of nerve pain (neuropathic pain).
Management of partial seizures.
dosage: As prescribed (dosage is usually increased gradually).
precautions: Do not stop suddenly. May cause mood or behavior changes.

name: Pregabalin (Lyrica)
description: Pregabalin is used to treat nerve pain, fibromyalgia, and certain types of seizures.
uses: Relief of nerve pain from diabetes or shingles.
Treatment of fibromyalgia and generalized anxiety disorder.
dosage: 75mg to 150mg twice daily.
precautions: May be habit-forming. Do not stop suddenly. Avoid alcohol.

name: Amitriptyline
description: Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant used to treat depression and nerve pain.
uses: Treatment of depression.
Prevention of migraines and relief of chronic nerve pain (off-label).
dosage: 10mg to 75mg daily at bedtime (lower doses for pain).
precautions: May cause drowsiness; avoid driving. Monitor for suicidal thoughts in young adults.

name: Escitalopram (Lexapro)
description: Escitalopram is an SSRI used to treat depression and anxiety.
uses: Treatment of major depressive disorder.
Treatment of generalized anxiety disorder.
dosage: 10mg to 20mg once daily.
precautions: Do not stop suddenly. May take several weeks to see full effect.

name: Naproxen (Synflex)
description: Naproxen is an NSAID used to reduce pain, inflammation, and fever.
uses: Relief of pain from arthritis, gout, menstrual cramps, and minor injuries.
dosage: 250mg to 500mg twice daily.
precautions: Take with food or milk. Avoid if you have stomach ulcers or heart disease.

name: Celecoxib (Celebrex)
description: Celecoxib is a COX-2 inhibitor (NSAID) used to treat pain and inflammation with less stomach irritation.
uses: Relief of pain and inflammation in arthritis and acute pain.
dosage: 100mg to 200mg once or twice daily.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have heart disease or a history of stomach ulcers.

name: Allopurinol (Zyloric)
description: Allopurinol is used to lower uric acid levels in the blood and prevent gout attacks.
uses: Prevention of gout attacks.
Prevention of kidney stones.
dosage: 100mg to 300mg once daily after a meal.
precautions: Drink plenty of fluids. Stop immediately and see a doctor if a rash develops.

name: Colchicine
description: Colchicine is used to prevent or treat gout attacks.
uses: Treatment of acute gout flares.
Prevention of gout attacks.
dosage: As prescribed (requires specific dosing for acute attacks).
precautions: Do not exceed the prescribed dose. Report severe diarrhea to your doctor.

name: Fexofenadine (Telfast)
description: Fexofenadine is a non-drowsy antihistamine used for allergy relief.
uses: Relief of hay fever symptoms (sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes).
Treatment of itchy skin rashes and hives.
dosage: 60mg twice daily or 120mg-180mg once daily.
precautions: Avoid taking with fruit juices (apple, orange, or grapefruit).

name: Betahistine (Serc)
description: Betahistine is used to treat symptoms of Meniere's disease such as vertigo and tinnitus.
uses: Relief of vertigo (dizziness).
Treatment of tinnitus (ringing in the ears) and hearing loss associated with Meniere's.
dosage: 8mg to 16mg three times daily.
precautions: Take with food to reduce stomach upset. Consult a doctor if you have asthma or stomach ulcers.

name: Hyoscine Hydrobromide (Travelmin)
description: Hyoscine hydrobromide is used to prevent motion sickness.
uses: Prevention of nausea and vomiting caused by motion sickness.
dosage: 0.3mg to 0.6mg 30-60 minutes before travel.
precautions: May cause significant drowsiness. Avoid alcohol and driving.

name: Simethicone (Air-X)
description: Simethicone is used to relieve symptoms of extra gas such as bloating and pressure.
uses: Relief of gas, bloating, and discomfort in the stomach and intestines.
dosage: 40mg to 125mg after meals and at bedtime.
precautions: Chew tablets thoroughly before swallowing.

name: Lactulose (Duphalac)
description: Lactulose is a synthetic sugar used to treat constipation.
uses: Treatment of chronic constipation.
Management of portal-systemic encephalopathy.
dosage: 15ml to 30ml daily, adjusted based on response.
precautions: May take 24-48 hours to work. Consult a doctor if you have diabetes.

name: Senna (Senokot)
description: Senna is a stimulant laxative used for short-term relief of constipation.
uses: Relief of occasional constipation.
dosage: 1-2 tablets at bedtime.
precautions: Do not use for more than 7 days without medical advice. Avoid if you have severe abdominal pain.

name: Bisacodyl (Dulcolax)
description: Bisacodyl is a stimulant laxative used to treat constipation or clear the bowels before surgery.
uses: Relief of constipation.
Bowel preparation for medical procedures.
dosage: 5mg to 10mg once daily, usually at bedtime.
precautions: Do not take within 1 hour of antacids or milk. Do not use daily for more than 5 days.

name: Spasmo-canulase
description: Spasmo-canulase is a combination medicine used to treat digestive disorders and bloating.
uses: Relief of digestive discomfort, gas, and bloating.
Improvement of digestion.
dosage: 1-2 capsules with meals.
precautions: Swallow capsules whole. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist.

name: Zinc Sulfate
description: Zinc sulfate is a mineral supplement used to treat and prevent zinc deficiency.
uses: Treatment of zinc deficiency.
Support for immune function and wound healing.
Management of diarrhea in children (with ORS).
dosage: As prescribed (varies by age and condition).
precautions: Best taken with food to reduce nausea. Do not exceed the recommended dose.

name: Folic Acid
description: Folic acid is a B-vitamin used to treat anemia and prevent birth defects.
uses: Prevention of neural tube defects during pregnancy.
Treatment of folic acid deficiency anemia.
dosage: 400mcg to 5mg daily depending on the condition.
side_effects: Rarely causes side effects at normal doses.
precautions: Consult a doctor for the appropriate dose during pregnancy.

name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
description: Vitamin C is an essential vitamin used to support the immune system and prevent scurvy.
uses: Prevention and treatment of vitamin C deficiency.
Support for immune health and skin repair.
dosage: 100mg to 1000mg daily.
side_effects: Stomach upset or diarrhea (at high doses).
precautions: High doses may increase the risk of kidney stones in some people.

name: Calcium Carbonate
description: Calcium carbonate is a mineral supplement used to prevent or treat low blood calcium levels.
uses: Support for bone health and prevention of osteoporosis.
Relief of heartburn and acid indigestion (as an antacid).
dosage: 500mg to 1200mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Best taken with food. Consult a doctor if you have kidney stones.

name: Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol)
description: Vitamin D3 is essential for calcium absorption and bone health.
uses: Prevention and treatment of vitamin D deficiency.
Support for bone and immune health.
dosage: 400IU to 2000IU daily, or as prescribed.
side_effects: Rarely causes side effects at normal doses.
precautions: High doses should be taken under medical supervision.

name: Mebeverine (Colofac)
description: Mebeverine is an antispasmodic used to treat irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
uses: Relief of stomach pain and cramps associated with IBS.
dosage: 135mg three times a day, 20 minutes before meals.
precautions: Consult a doctor if symptoms change or worsen.

name: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu)
description: Oseltamivir is an antiviral medication used to treat and prevent influenza (flu).
uses: Treatment of flu symptoms if started within 48 hours of onset.
Prevention of flu in people exposed to the virus.
dosage: 75mg twice daily for 5 days for treatment.
precautions: Not a substitute for the flu vaccine. Complete the full course.

name: Metoclopramide (Maxolon)
description: Metoclopramide is used to treat nausea, vomiting, and heartburn.
uses: Relief of nausea and vomiting.
Treatment of GERD and slow stomach emptying (gastroparesis).
dosage: 10mg three times a day, 30 minutes before meals.
precautions: Do not use for more than 5 days. Avoid alcohol.

name: Hydroxyzine (Atarax)
description: Hydroxyzine is an antihistamine used to treat itching and anxiety.
uses: Relief of itching caused by allergies.
Treatment of short-term anxiety and tension.
Sedation before surgery.
dosage: 25mg to 50mg three to four times daily.
precautions: Highly sedating; avoid driving. Consult a doctor if you have heart rhythm issues.

name: Miconazole (Daktarin)
description: Miconazole is an antifungal medication used for skin and oral fungal infections.
uses: Treatment of athlete's foot, ringworm, and oral thrush.
Treatment of vaginal yeast infections.
dosage: Apply cream twice daily. Use oral gel after meals.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes. Inform your doctor if you are taking blood thinners like warfarin.

name: Silver Sulfadiazine (Flammazine)
description: Silver sulfadiazine is a topical antibiotic used to prevent and treat infections in burns.
uses: Prevention and treatment of infection in second- and third-degree burns.
dosage: Apply to the cleaned burn area 1-2 times daily.
precautions: Do not use during late pregnancy or on premature infants. Consult a doctor if a rash develops.

name: Mupirocin (Bactroban)
description: Mupirocin is a topical antibiotic used to treat skin infections like impetigo.
uses: Treatment of bacterial skin infections (impetigo, folliculitis).
Elimination of MRSA from the nose.
dosage: Apply a small amount to the affected area 3 times daily for up to 10 days.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes. Consult a doctor if no improvement in 3-5 days.

name: Permethrin (Scaboma)
description: Permethrin is used to treat scabies and head lice.
uses: Treatment of scabies (skin mites).
Treatment of head lice.
dosage: Apply cream/lotion thoroughly from neck to toes and wash off after 8-14 hours.
precautions: All family members may need treatment. Wash all clothing and bedding in hot water.

name: Terbinafine (Lamisil)
description: Terbinafine is an antifungal used to treat skin and nail infections.
uses: Treatment of athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm.
Treatment of fungal nail infections.
dosage: Apply cream 1-2 times daily. Oral tablets as prescribed.
precautions: Oral use requires liver function monitoring. Continue topical treatment for recommended duration.

name: Koffy Syrup
description: Koffy is a common cough syrup in Myanmar used to relieve various types of cough.
uses: Relief of dry cough and productive cough.
Soothing an irritated throat.
dosage: Adults: 10ml to 15ml three times a day.
precautions: May cause drowsiness. Consult a doctor if cough persists for more than a week.

name: Sunkist (Vitamin C)
description: Sunkist is a popular Vitamin C supplement in Myanmar.
uses: Boosting the immune system.
Prevention of Vitamin C deficiency.
dosage: One tablet daily.
precautions: Do not exceed the recommended dose.

name: Tiger Balm
description: Tiger Balm is a topical ointment used for pain relief.
uses: Relief of muscle aches and pains.
Relief of tension headaches (apply to temples).
Relief of itchiness from insect bites.
dosage: Rub gently over the affected area 3-4 times daily.
side_effects: Skin irritation or redness in some people.
precautions: For external use only. Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.

name: Zam-Buk
description: Zam-Buk is a traditional medicated ointment.
uses: Relief of minor cuts, burns, and bruises.
Relief of insect bites and itchy skin.
dosage: Apply to the affected area as needed.
precautions: For external use only.

name: Eno
description: Eno is an effervescent fruit salt used as an antacid.
uses: Rapid relief of acidity, heartburn, and indigestion.
dosage: One sachet (5g) dissolved in a glass of water. Do not take more than 2 doses a day.
precautions: Not suitable for people on a low-sodium diet. Consult a doctor if you have kidney or heart problems.

name: Traditional Medicine No. 1 (Digestive)
description: A common Myanmar traditional medicine for digestion.
uses: Relief of indigestion, stomach bloating, and loss of appetite.
dosage: 1-2 tablets or 1/2 teaspoon of powder after meals.
precautions: Consult a traditional medicine practitioner for prolonged use.

name: Traditional Medicine No. 2 (Anti-flatulence)
description: Myanmar traditional medicine used for relieving gas and wind.
uses: Relief of flatulence, dizziness, and body aches attributed to 'wind' in traditional medicine.
dosage: As directed on the package, usually twice daily.
precautions: Keep in a cool, dry place.

name: Traditional Medicine No. 16 (Heat Relief)
description: Myanmar traditional medicine used to balance body heat.
uses: Relief of symptoms attributed to 'excessive heat' such as sore throat, mouth ulcers, and constipation.
dosage: One tablet or small amount of powder twice daily.
precautions: Consult a practitioner if symptoms persist.

name: Methycobal (Mecobalamin)
description: Methycobal is a form of vitamin B12 used to treat peripheral neuropathies and megaloblastic anemia.
uses: Treatment of peripheral neuropathies (nerve damage).
Treatment of megaloblastic anemia due to vitamin B12 deficiency.
dosage: 500mcg three times a day, or as prescribed by a doctor.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Long-term use requires monitoring.

name: Warfarin (Panwarfin)
description: Warfarin is an anticoagulant (blood thinner) used to prevent blood clots.
uses: Prevention of blood clots in the legs, lungs, and heart.
Reducing the risk of stroke and heart attack.
dosage: As prescribed (requires regular blood tests to monitor INR).
precautions: Avoid activities that may cause injury. Maintain a consistent intake of vitamin K-rich foods (green leafy vegetables). Consult a doctor before taking other medicines.

name: Insulin (Human Insulin)
description: Insulin is used to control blood sugar in people with diabetes.
uses: Treatment of type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage: As prescribed (injected subcutaneously).
side_effects: Swelling or itching at the injection site
precautions: Monitor blood sugar regularly. Learn the signs of hypoglycemia and how to treat it.

name: Valsartan (Diovan)
description: Valsartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure.
uses: Treatment of hypertension.
Treatment of heart failure.
Improving survival after a heart attack.
dosage: 40mg to 320mg once daily.
side_effects: Cough (less common than with ACE inhibitors)
precautions: Do not use during pregnancy. Monitor kidney function and potassium levels.

name: Metoprolol (Betaloc)
description: Metoprolol is a beta-blocker used to treat high blood pressure, chest pain, and heart failure.
uses: Treatment of hypertension.
Prevention of angina (chest pain).
Improving survival after a heart attack.
dosage: 25mg to 200mg once or twice daily.
precautions: Do not stop taking abruptly. Consult a doctor if you have asthma.

name: Diazepam (Valium)
description: Diazepam is a benzodiazepine used to treat anxiety, muscle spasms, and seizures.
uses: Short-term relief of anxiety.
Relief of muscle spasms.
Management of seizures and alcohol withdrawal.
dosage: 2mg to 10mg two to four times daily (as prescribed).
precautions: High potential for addiction and dependence. Avoid alcohol. Do not drive while taking this medicine.

name: Alprazolam (Xanax)
description: Alprazolam is used to treat anxiety and panic disorders.
uses: Short-term management of anxiety disorders.
Treatment of panic disorder.
dosage: 0.25mg to 0.5mg three times daily (as prescribed).
precautions: May be habit-forming. Do not stop suddenly. Avoid alcohol.

name: Digoxin (Lanoxin)
description: Digoxin is used to treat heart failure and certain types of irregular heartbeats.
uses: Management of heart failure.
Control of heart rate in atrial fibrillation.
dosage: 0.125mg to 0.25mg once daily (as prescribed).
precautions: Requires regular monitoring of blood levels and heart rate. Report signs of toxicity (nausea, vision changes) to a doctor.

name: Isosorbide Dinitrate (Isordil)
description: Isosorbide dinitrate is a nitrate used to prevent chest pain (angina).
uses: Prevention of angina attacks.
Treatment of chronic heart failure (with other drugs).
dosage: 5mg to 40mg two to three times daily.
precautions: Do not use with medications for erectile dysfunction (e.g., sildenafil). Sit or lie down if feeling dizzy.

name: Prednisone
description: Prednisone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress the immune system.
uses: Treatment of allergic reactions, asthma, and autoimmune diseases.
Treatment of inflammatory conditions like arthritis.
dosage: 5mg to 60mg per day (dosage varies widely).
precautions: May mask signs of infection. Do not stop suddenly if used for a long period.

name: Hydrocortisone (Skin Cream)
description: Hydrocortisone is a mild corticosteroid used to reduce skin inflammation and itching.
uses: Relief of itching and inflammation from insect bites, eczema, and rashes.
dosage: Apply thinly to the affected area 2 to 4 times daily.
precautions: Avoid use on the face or broken skin unless directed by a doctor.

name: Moxifloxacin (Vigamox)
description: Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections, including eye infections.
uses: Treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis (pink eye).
Treatment of respiratory infections (oral form).
dosage: One drop in the affected eye 3 times a day.
precautions: Do not wear contact lenses while you have signs of a bacterial eye infection.

name: Tamsulosin (Harnal)
description: Tamsulosin is used to treat symptoms of an enlarged prostate (BPH).
uses: Improving urination in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia.
dosage: 0.4mg once daily, 30 minutes after the same meal each day.
precautions: May cause a drop in blood pressure when standing up. Consult a doctor before cataract surgery.

name: Finasteride (Proscar)
description: Finasteride is used to treat enlarged prostate and male pattern hair loss.
uses: Treatment of symptoms of BPH.
Treatment of male pattern baldness (at lower doses).
dosage: 1mg to 5mg once daily.
precautions: Pregnant women should not handle crushed tablets as it can affect a male fetus.

name: Sildenafil (Viagra)
description: Sildenafil is used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
uses: Treatment of erectile dysfunction.
Improving exercise capacity in pulmonary hypertension.
dosage: 25mg to 100mg as needed, about 1 hour before sexual activity.
precautions: Do not use with nitrates for chest pain. Seek emergency help if an erection lasts more than 4 hours.

name: Levofloxacin (Cravit)
description: Levofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections.
uses: Treatment of pneumonia, sinus infections, and urinary tract infections.
Treatment of skin infections and chronic bronchitis.
dosage: 250mg to 750mg once daily for 7 to 14 days.
precautions: Drink plenty of fluids. Avoid excessive sun exposure. Not recommended for children or pregnant women.

name: Gliclazide (Diamicron)
description: Gliclazide is an oral hypoglycemic medicine used to treat type 2 diabetes.
uses: Control of blood sugar levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage: 30mg to 120mg once daily with breakfast.
precautions: Monitor blood sugar regularly. Carry a sugar source in case of hypoglycemia.

name: Spironolactone (Aldactone)
description: Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic used to treat high blood pressure and fluid retention.
uses: Treatment of heart failure and liver cirrhosis edema.
Treatment of hypertension and hyperaldosteronism.
dosage: 25mg to 100mg daily.
precautions: Avoid potassium supplements. Monitor kidney function and potassium levels.

name: Carvedilol (Dilatrend)
description: Carvedilol is a beta-blocker used to treat heart failure and high blood pressure.
uses: Management of congestive heart failure.
Treatment of hypertension.
dosage: 3.125mg to 25mg twice daily.
precautions: Do not stop suddenly. Take with food to reduce the risk of low blood pressure.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ)
description: Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic (water pill) used to treat high blood pressure.
uses: Treatment of hypertension.
Treatment of edema caused by heart failure or kidney disease.
dosage: 12.5mg to 50mg once daily.
precautions: May cause potassium loss. Use sunscreen as it may increase sun sensitivity.

name: Candesartan (Blopress)
description: Candesartan is an ARB used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure.
uses: Treatment of hypertension.
Management of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
dosage: 8mg to 32mg once daily.
precautions: Do not use during pregnancy. Monitor kidney function regularly.

name: Sitagliptin + Metformin (Janumet)
description: A combination medicine used to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes.
uses: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus when single agent therapy is insufficient.
dosage: One tablet twice daily with meals.
precautions: Risk of lactic acidosis (rare but serious). Monitor kidney function.

name: Clarithromycin (Klacid)
description: Clarithromycin is a macrolide antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections.
uses: Treatment of throat, sinus, and lung infections.
Treatment of skin infections and stomach ulcers (with other drugs).
dosage: 250mg to 500mg twice daily for 7 to 14 days.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have heart rhythm disorders. Many drug interactions.

name: Loratadine (Claritin)
description: Loratadine is a non-drowsy antihistamine used to treat allergy symptoms.
uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes.
Treatment of hives and skin allergies.
dosage: 10mg once daily.
precautions: Generally non-drowsy, but use caution if performing tasks requiring alertness.

name: Cetirizine (Zyrtec)
description: Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to treat cold and allergy symptoms.
uses: Relief of hay fever and allergy symptoms.
Treatment of itching and swelling caused by hives.
dosage: 5mg to 10mg once daily.
precautions: May cause drowsiness. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine.

name: Domperidone (Motilium)
description: Domperidone is an anti-sickness medicine used to treat nausea and vomiting.
uses: Relief of nausea and vomiting.
Treatment of stomach discomfort and bloating.
dosage: 10mg up to 3 times a day, 30 minutes before meals.
precautions: Not for long-term use. Consult a doctor if you have heart conditions.

name: Ranitidine (Zantac)
description: Ranitidine is an H2 blocker used to reduce stomach acid.
uses: Treatment of heartburn, acid reflux, and stomach ulcers.
dosage: 150mg twice daily or 300mg at bedtime.
precautions: Consult a doctor if symptoms persist for more than 2 weeks.

name: Pantoprazole (Controloc)
description: Pantoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor used to treat acid-related stomach and throat problems.
uses: Treatment of GERD and erosive esophagitis.
Prevention of stomach ulcers.
dosage: 20mg to 40mg once daily before breakfast.
precautions: Long-term use may affect vitamin B12 absorption and bone density.

name: Bisacodyl (Dulcolax)
description: Bisacodyl is a stimulant laxative used to treat constipation.
uses: Short-term relief of occasional constipation.
Bowel preparation before surgery or medical procedures.
dosage: 5mg to 10mg once daily at bedtime.
precautions: Do not take with milk or antacids. Do not use for more than 5 days without medical advice.

name: Loperamide (Imodium)
description: Loperamide is used to treat sudden diarrhea.
uses: Symptomatic relief of acute diarrhea.
dosage: 4mg initially, then 2mg after each loose stool. Maximum 16mg per day.
precautions: Do not use if you have bloody stools or fever. Drink plenty of fluids.

name: Hyoscine (Buscopan)
description: Hyoscine is an antispasmodic used to relieve stomach and intestinal cramps.
uses: Relief of abdominal cramps and spasms.
Treatment of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) symptoms.
dosage: 10mg to 20mg three to four times daily.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have glaucoma or an enlarged prostate.

name: Mebeverine (Colofac)
description: Mebeverine is used to treat symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
uses: Relief of abdominal pain, cramps, and bloating associated with IBS.
dosage: 135mg three times a day, 20 minutes before meals.
side_effects: Rarely causes side effects. May cause a rash.
precautions: Consult a doctor if symptoms worsen or change.

name: Dicycloverine (Bentyl)
description: Dicycloverine is used to treat functional bowel/irritable bowel syndrome.
uses: Relief of stomach and intestinal spasms.
dosage: 10mg to 20mg four times daily.
precautions: May cause drowsiness. Avoid use in infants under 6 months.

name: Simethicone (Air-X)
description: Simethicone is used to relieve the painful symptoms of too much gas in the stomach and intestines.
uses: Relief of pressure, bloating, and gas (flatulence).
dosage: 40mg to 125mg after meals and at bedtime.
precautions: Chew tablets thoroughly before swallowing.

name: Calcium + Vitamin D3
description: A combination supplement for bone health.
uses: Prevention and treatment of osteoporosis.
Calcium and Vitamin D deficiency.
dosage: One tablet daily or as prescribed.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you have kidney stones.

name: Cetzy (Cetirizine)
description: Cetzy is a brand of Cetirizine, an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms.
uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, and watery eyes.
Treatment of itchy skin rashes and hives.
dosage: One 10mg tablet once daily.
precautions: May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you.

name: V.Rohto (Vitamin Eye Drops)
description: V.Rohto contains various vitamins and amino acids to relieve eye fatigue and redness.
uses: Relief of eye strain and tiredness.
Reduction of eye redness and irritation caused by dust or sweat.
dosage: Instill 2 to 3 drops, 5 to 6 times daily.
precautions: Do not use while wearing soft contact lenses. If irritation persists, consult a doctor.

name: Tears Naturale (Artificial Tears)
description: Tears Naturale is a lubricant eye drop used to relieve dry and irritated eyes.
uses: Relief of burning and irritation due to dryness of the eye.
Protection against further irritation.
dosage: Instill 1 or 2 drops in the affected eye(s) as needed.
precautions: Discard the container 30 days after opening. If you experience eye pain or vision changes, stop use.

name: Gentamicin (Antibiotic Eye Drops)
description: Gentamicin is an antibiotic eye drop used to treat bacterial infections of the eye.
uses: Treatment of conjunctivitis (pink eye).
Treatment of other superficial bacterial eye infections.
dosage: Instill 1 to 2 drops every 4 hours into the affected eye.
precautions: Use for the full prescribed duration even if symptoms improve. Do not touch the dropper tip to any surface.

name: Amoxicillin (Amoxil)
description: Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic that fights bacteria.
uses: Treatment of infections of the ear, nose, throat, urinary tract, and skin.
dosage: Usually 250mg to 500mg every 8 hours or 500mg to 875mg every 12 hours.
precautions: Do not use if you are allergic to penicillin. Complete the full course.

name: Omeprazole (Prilosec / Losec)
description: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that decreases the amount of acid produced in the stomach.
uses: Treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
Stomach ulcers
Heartburn
dosage: Usually 20mg once daily before a meal.
precautions: Take 30-60 minutes before breakfast for best results.

name: Gaviscon (Antacid)
description: Gaviscon is an antacid that provides fast relief from heartburn and acid indigestion.
uses: Relief of heartburn
Acid reflux
Indigestion after meals
dosage: 10-20ml of liquid or 2-4 tablets after meals and at bedtime.
precautions: If symptoms persist for more than 7 days, consult a doctor.

name: Neurobion (Vitamin B1+B6+B12)
description: Neurobion is a combination of three essential neurotropic B vitamins.
uses: Treatment of vitamin B deficiency
Relief of nerve pain, numbness, and tingling.
dosage: One tablet 1-3 times daily.
precautions: Consult a doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.

name: Decolgen (Cold & Flu)
description: Decolgen is a combined medicine for the relief of common cold and flu symptoms.
uses: Relief of nasal congestion
Runny nose
Headache
Fever
dosage: One tablet every 4 to 6 hours.
precautions: May cause drowsiness. Do not drive or operate machinery.

name: Amlodipine (Norvasc)
description: Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker used to treat high blood pressure.
uses: Treatment of high blood pressure (hypertension)
Prevention of chest pain (angina).
dosage: Usually 5mg once daily, can be increased to 10mg.
precautions: Check blood pressure regularly. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Atorvastatin (Lipitor)
description: Atorvastatin is a statin medicine used to lower cholesterol.
uses: Prevention of cardiovascular disease
Lowering high cholesterol and triglycerides.
dosage: 10mg to 80mg once daily.
precautions: Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice. Take at the same time each day.

name: Burmeton (Chlorpheniramine)
description: Burmeton is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms.
uses: Relief of runny nose
Sneezing
Itchy eyes
Allergic skin reactions.
dosage: 4mg every 4 to 6 hours.
precautions: Causes significant drowsiness. Avoid alcohol.
